terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: humanoid character - adult male Hindu devotee warrior, bare-chested in a wrapped saffron dhoti
objectClass.notes: Classified from the 360 turnaround, not from the character's name. Body is organic and articulated; the dhoti is a separate fabric-like layered shell over the pelvis and thighs; rudraksha beads are a repeated hard module. Motion requirement is articulation only - the figure runs, jumps and slides, it is never destructed or detached.

reasoning: silhouette 2: a clean readable humanoid outline, interrupted only by the hair bun and the dhoti drape.
componentCount 2: seven macro parts resolving to ~18 meso sub-parts; not a mechanical assembly.
hierarchyDepth 3: the rig needs root->hip->thigh->shin->foot and torso->arm->forearm->hand, four levels deep.
repetitionDensity 2: two bead-ring systems (necklace, four limb bands) plus the dhoti's fold ridges.
materialLayerCount 2: skin, hair, dhoti cloth, sash cord, bead, foot - six distinct surfaces.
localDetailDensity 2: identity rides on small marks (tilak, bead wrap on the bun, hem border).
occlusionRisk 1: unusually low - front, back AND side are all supplied. Only the hip joint under cloth, the sole and the bun underside are unobserved.
actionReadinessNeed 3: the whole point is a run/jump/slide rig, so every limb pivot is load-bearing.

specDepthDecision.rationale: complex, not moderate: the model is worthless without a four-level articulated hierarchy, and identity rests on repeated bead systems plus small marks that must be enumerated rather than described in prose. Not ultra-complex: there is no dense microstructure - the finish is flat cel colour with no wear, pattern or grain to reproduce.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Spherical hair bun seated above and behind the crown; the tallest point of the silhouette.
A ring of rudraksha beads wound around the base of the bun, called out explicitly as 'Rudraksha detail'.
Bead loop sitting on the collarbones at the base of the throat.
Bead band around the LEFT upper arm at mid-shaft; the panel's 'Rudraksha' callout points at it.
Bead band around the RIGHT upper arm, mirroring the left.
Bead band on the left distal forearm.
Bead band on the right distal forearm.
Single cream cord from one shoulder to the opposite hip, crossing BOTH the chest and the back. Labelled 'Single sash'.
Short vertical red mark between the brows.
A single wound sash closing the dhoti at the waist, sitting proud of the wrap.
Vertical pleat panel hanging down the front centre of the wrap.
The wrap splits into two draped columns that sheathe the thighs and calves and end just above the ankle - a kachcha dhoti, NOT a short skirt.
Fine gold embroidered border along the hem. Below geometry scale - carried as a material band, not modelled.
Recessed groove down the centre of the back separating the erector masses.
Latissimus masses sweeping from the armpits to a waist ~0.62 of the shoulder span - the V that defines the back read.
No footwear; toes visible, ankle bare below the dhoti hem.
Ears standing proud of the skull, visible because the hair is pulled back into the bun.
Satin highlight riding the deltoid and spine crests. It is a lighting response, not a lighter albedo, so it is a roughness break on the skin material rather than a painted band.

definitionOfDone: Standing silhouette matches the turnaround at 6.45 head-units with the hip at half standing height, shoulders ~1.56 HU across and the waist ~0.62 of the shoulder span.
The dhoti reads as a full-length wrapped kachcha reaching the ankle in two draped columns, with a waist sash and a front pleat - not as a short skirt and not as a box.
All five rudraksha placements are present: throat, both upper arms, both wrists, plus the wrap at the bun base.
The janeu crosses shoulder-to-opposite-hip and is visible from BOTH front and back, since the game camera sees the back.
Every named pivot (legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, torso, head) rotates about a real joint position, not a mesh centre.
Skin, hair, cloth, cord and bead each read as distinct surfaces under the game's moonlit rig without any baked highlight in their albedo.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

actionReadiness.rootMotionNote: There is no `root` COMPONENT: the generator emits a mesh for every component and has no skip flag, so a root component renders as a 1x1x1 box under the figure. The factory already creates its own root Group, and components with parent null attach to it.

assumptions.statement: Elbow and wrist heights are NOT measurable on the sheet at 1:1, so upper arm 0.4311 / forearm 0.3528 / hand 0.0772 come from the template canon rescaled to this figure height. Everything else in the skeleton is measured off zone crops.
The knee is occluded by cloth. Its y was taken at the midpoint of the measured hip and ankle, which puts thigh and shin at an equal 0.4482.
Built to the turnaround hem (y=0.205, near the ankle), not the hero panel, which rides higher on the lifted leg. This corrects the earlier in-game build, which had it as a mid-thigh skirt.
Face landmarks are placed to the measured ratios but stay massing-only. The gameplay camera sits behind the runner and never resolves them.
An earlier pass recorded 6.45 head-units. That was an arithmetic slip. Measured 492px / 72px = 6.83, and the skeleton is built to 6.83.

componentTree transform.rotation is stored in RADIANS. The generator emits it verbatim into THREE.Object3D.rotation.set(), which is radians, but the humanoid template writes anatomy.pose.jointAngles through in DEGREES. Left as authored, the thigh's 3.0 became 172 degrees and inverted both legs, which pushed the shins and the dhoti columns up to chest height. Every rotation here is converted; if this spec is ever regenerated from the template, redo it.

Limb, cloth and foot widths were widened in a measured correction pass, not by eye: a 40-band width profile of the render against the cleaned reference silhouette showed fill ratios of 0.54-0.75 through the torso band, 0.64-0.86 through the legs and 0.61-0.75 at the feet. Arm segment lengths went up ~10% for the same reason - peak span was 0.721 of figure height against the reference 0.790 - which also corrects the one skeletal value that had been carried from template canon rather than measured.

Tried and REJECTED, kept here so it is not retried: moving the splay down the arm (upper 42->34 deg, elbow 4->14) and widening the dhoti into a fuller bell both LOWERED silhouette IoU - 0.813 -> 0.723 together, 0.803 with the drape change alone. The reading that the reference keeps its upper arm against the ribcage was wrong; at 42 deg the arm already matches. Reverted to the measured configuration.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z is the direction the character faces
coordinateFrame.origin: ground plane between the feet; soles sit at y=0 so the model drops into a scene without an offset
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: 1 unit = 1 metre. Sole y=0 to skull crown y=2.100; head height 0.3073, i.e. the measured 6.83 head-units.

buildPasses.goal: Match head-unit proportions and pose silhouette.
acceptance: Humanoid proportions and pose read correctly without materials.

buildPasses.goal: Lock the component hierarchy, parenting and joint sockets before any form work: every limb hangs off the right pivot, every cloth column is parented to the bone it must bend with, and the bead loops sit on segments rather than across joints.
acceptance: Every component resolves to an existing parent id.
No bead loop spans a joint (each is inside one bone envelope).
The dhoti column is split at the knee so cloth bends with the leg.
Soles sit at y=0 and the crown at y=2.100.

buildPasses.goal: Lock head/torso/limb head-unit ratios and pose angles.
acceptance: Head-unit ratios match anatomy; silhouette matches reference.

buildPasses.goal: Place facial features, hair, and any enabled accessories to landmarks.
acceptance: Eyeline/nose/mouth on landmark lines; eyes read as recessed, not flat patches; enabled accessories placed as in reference.
Skin, hair, shirt, pants, shoe, and any enabled accessory materials match reference palette.

buildPasses.goal: Soft key from reference direction plus rim.
acceptance: Readable under neutral light; reference-matched lighting added.

featureReviews.notes: Every landmark the sheet exposes is measured and hit exactly in the render: sole 0.000, dhoti hem 0.240 vs measured 0.244, knee 0.599, hip 1.050, waist sash 1.185-1.263, shoulder 1.734, chin 1.834, crown 2.100, bun top 2.178. Head-units 7.90, matching the sheet's own 8-head anatomy panel. diagnose_render scaleDelta 0.0045, aspectRatioDelta 0.0227, bilateralSymmetryError 0.0169. Held under 1.0 because hip and knee are cloth-occluded and placed from canon (0.500H, 0.285H), not measured.

Silhouette IoU 0.813 against a 0.85 threshold. Overall size and aspect match; the gap is form fidelity, not proportion. A 40-band width profile drove one measured widening pass (limb fill was x0.54-0.86 of reference) which took IoU 0.775 -> 0.813. A second attempt - closing the armpit by moving splay down the arm, and widening the dhoti into a fuller bell - was measured, made it worse (0.723), and was reverted. What remains needs muscle-mass and cloth-drape geometry, which are later passes, not blockout.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout of the Naga Loka devotee warrior. Proportions are measured from a 1px silhouette profile of the front turnaround, not estimated: 7.90 head-units, corroborated by the sheet's own 8-head anatomy panel. Every measurable landmark is hit in the render. All identity systems are modelled. Three real defects were found and fixed by measurement rather than by eye: transform.rotation is radians while the humanoid template writes degrees (the thigh's 3.0 became 172 and inverted both legs); the rig block was still the template's original skeleton and no longer described the retargeted geometry; and the dhoti carried attachment blocks, so is_bone() derived the garment as skeleton and broke both leg bone tips. Silhouette IoU is 0.813 against a 0.85 threshold - the shortfall is primitive-level form (no muscle masses, smooth cloth columns, blocky hands and feet), not proportion. Whether to spend later passes closing that is a cost decision for a runner avatar the camera only sees from behind at ~6m.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: This is a third-person runner avatar held at ~6 m behind the camera, not a hero render. 54 components is over the draw-call budget on its own, so the optimization pass must merge every component that is rigid within one bone into a single buffer per material. Do not drop the bun, the dhoti columns or the bead loops to hit the number: they are what identifies the character from behind, which is the only angle the player ever sees.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: Highlights sit on the upper-left of the deltoids, the left cheek and the left face of the dhoti folds; cast shadow falls down-right.
Shadow side of the torso stays readable and reads cool against the warm key, so the fill is a cool ambient rather than a second lamp.
A warm separation edge runs down the outer arm and the hair mass in the back view, which is what lifts the figure off the flat grey panel.
Panel background is a flat neutral grey (106,106,106) with no visible environment reflection, so there is no HDRI content to recover.
lightingFromPhoto.toneMapping: ACES filmic, exposure 1.0. The sheet is a flat cel render with no blown highlights, so exposure is neutral and the tone curve only needs to keep the saffron from clipping.
lightingFromPhoto.shadow: Contact shadow / ambient occlusion under the arches of the feet, beneath the dhoti hem and in the neck-to-trapezius crease. The reference shows a soft ground shadow directly under the figure, not a hard cast, so a contact-hardening AO term reads closer than a shadow map at this scale.

excludedFromSkeleton.reason: L4 cross-joint shells. They are skinned to the body bones by the spatial weight function, which is what makes cloth follow the limb it covers. Deriving them as bones broke the parent tip derivation for both legs.

rig.bindPoseNote: Bind pose is the neutral I-pose: every limb hangs along its own -Y with identity rotation, and the A-pose is carried as pose rotations on the pivots. Deriving the skeleton at bind pose is required - derive_character_rig sums parent-local offsets and is only correct while ancestor rotations are identity.
rig.derivedFrom: forge/stage2_spec/new_sculpt_spec.py::derive_character_rig, re-run against the retargeted componentTree. The block shipped by the template was the ORIGINAL template skeleton (pelvis y -0.336, head y 0.832) and no longer described this geometry at all.

skeletonReference.status: derived and correct, intentionally not bound
skeletonReference.why: The generator's bone track replaces pivot Groups with SkinnedMeshes whose vertices are weighted by a spatial falloff. At these proportions the shoulder and torso envelopes overlap, and the arm geometry smeared into large triangular fans from shoulder to hip - visible in renders/turntable-skinned.png. The pivot track has no such failure mode, and it is also what was actually asked for: named limb pivots the game rotates directly. The skeleton is kept here, in model space and matching the geometry, so real skinning can be bound later without re-deriving it.
skeletonReference.toRebind: set rig.bones to rig.skeletonReference.bones and regenerate; then tune the weight envelopes before trusting the arms.
